summary.intent: Plan and then execute Phase 69 of CipherBox (porting the node/v3 model to the Rust FUSE/WinFsp desktop stack with grant-root awareness), running end-to-end via GSD's plan-phase/execute-phase workflows with minimal user re-prompting, and ultimately ensure the work is validated by a real desktop-e2e run rather than just compile-green.
summary.outcome: Phase 69 grew from 14 to 25 plans across three rounds of in-execution architectural rescoping; 19/20 of the original plans (foundation, the atomic 11-slice FUSE cutover, JournalOp reshape, grant-scope gate, recycle-bin/vault-creation migration, legacy-type deletion) merged with a green workspace. A further gap was found (desktop still on legacy v2 vault-blob, incompatible with node/v3), triggering a 5-plan vault-blob-v3 port (69-21–69-25), of which 69-21/22/23 landed green by session's end. WinFsp (69-14) remains deferred to the user's Windows machine, and desktop-e2e has not yet been run as the completion gate.

repo: D-04 in CipherBox mandates a clean flag-day cutover — no dual read/write model may coexist; this forbids workspace-green intermediate states for the parts of a migration that must land atomically.
D-07 requires dual-keying: read plane refs (SealedChildRef) keyed by ipnsName, write plane refs (WriteChildRef) keyed by a childId UUID (derived via uuid_from_ino) — the two must never be conflated.

Terminal-owner zeroization rule: parent_read_key/parent_write_key are passed by borrow (&[u8]) so the type system (not just convention) prevents an executor from zeroing a caller-owned buffer; only self-minted keys get zeroed.

SC#6 requires exactly one gated read entrypoint (list_folder/list_folder_owned/fetch_node_gated) in crates/fuse; enforced via a CI grep gate with `// sc6-allow:` markers for legitimate exceptions (recycle-bin, vault-export, 69-13 reencrypt, replay).

The web (TS) side already shipped the real node/v3 root-key model in #578/#587/#588: vault blob v3 stores two independent random 32-byte keys (rootReadKey/rootWriteKey) ECIES-wrapped under the user pubkey, while the root Ed25519 IPNS keypair is HKDF-derived (not stored in the blob). The Rust desktop stack had NOT been updated to match and was silently incompatible with web-created vaults.

crates/fuse InodeKind is a read-WRITE vault-owner structure (holds ipns_private_key to sign records), unlike the web's 68.2 read-only mirror — this made the 'mechanical flip' assumption from research wrong twice.

Frozen cross-language KAT vectors (tests/vectors/*.json, e.g. vault-v3-blob.json, node-codec.json) are the authoritative byte-format oracle and are loaded at runtime in Rust tests via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, not hardcoded — always wire new codecs against them rather than re-deriving format independently.

cargo fmt run at a crate root (e.g. via `rustfmt lib.rs`) recursively reformats the whole module tree including unrelated pre-existing drift; every executor in this session had to `git checkout --` the out-of-scope reformatted files before committing.

code.finding: Desktop bridges node/v3 root_read_key/root_write_key from the legacy root_folder_key via `^ 0xA5` — a placeholder that must be deleted once real v3 vault-blob recovery is wired (plan 69-24).

JournalOp does NOT contain a `parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` field as research initially claimed — that field lives in the fuse-side MkdirJournalResult struct; the 'cross-crate weld' framing that justified atomicity in the first FUSE-cutover research was stale/incorrect.

list_folder_owned recovers per-node {read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key} through the same SC#6 gate as list_folder, enabling the FUSE mount (a read-write owner) to materialize a writable tree — this API did not exist until plan 69-17.

vault-blob-v3 codec format: 0x03 | u16_BE(readLen) | ECIES(rootReadKey) | u16_BE(writeLen) | ECIES(rootWriteKey), envelope-only (no crypto inside the codec); v2 codec is preserved untouched alongside it.

workflow: GSD's commit-helper tool reports `commit_failed` as a false negative even when the commit actually lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1` rather than retrying the commit.
Worktree executors sometimes misreport `expected_base` as their own last docs commit instead of the true fork point — verify via `git merge-base <worktree-branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.

When an atomic plan cannot reach a single green checkpoint in one executor session, decompose it into a bounded multi-session 'grind': dispatch fresh non-isolated executors onto the SAME branch, have each land incremental (possibly RED) commits, and record carry-forward facts in a committed runbook file so the grind survives usage-limit interruptions.

When two plans must land as one combined unit to preserve a 'workspace-green after every merge' invariant (e.g. an sdk-green/workspace-red plan followed by the plan that consumes it), continue the second plan's executor on the first plan's branch rather than merging the first alone.

For deep, unverifiable-in-isolation crypto/architecture work, prefer having an autonomous executor honestly halt with an evidence-backed blocker (zero edits, clean revert) over forcing speculative code to compile — then independently re-verify its central claims (grep counts, blast radius) before accepting or escalating to the user.
Session/usage limits manifest as agent task failures with a specific reset time; treat these as retry-later events (re-dispatch identical work after the reset), not as architectural or scope signals.

friction: gsd-planner crashed mid-run twice (API error mid-stream during initial planning of 69-14, and again on 69-16), requiring filesystem-fallback recovery by inspecting partial disk state and resuming with a fresh single-plan executor.

The atomic FUSE cutover plan (69-09) was halted THREE separate times by successive, deeper architectural discoveries (read/write coupling wider than scoped; no Node write-plane emit API existed; InodeKind is read-write not read-only and lacks a materialization API) — each requiring a new research+plan detour before execution could resume.
One 69-09 executor died mid-exploration purely from hitting the account's session usage limit (reset 2pm Berlin), initially indistinguishable from an architectural blocker until inspected.

The atomic 69-09 flip ultimately required an 11-slice, multi-session 'grind' (spanning a further session-limit reset at 7pm Berlin) because no compiling sub-unit existed for a ~12,300 LOC crypto-model migration.

Legacy folder-model types (FolderMetadata, FilePointer, etc.) turned out to still be load-bearing for the recycle-bin, vault-export, and vault-creation subsystems, invalidating plan 69-10's original 'delete all legacy types' premise and requiring two more migration plans (69-19, 69-20) before deletion was safe.

Even after the full non-Windows phase was reported complete (19/20 plans, workspace green), the user identified that the desktop was still using a placeholder root-key bridge (`^0xA5`), meaning desktop-e2e — the intended real validation gate — could not meaningfully run, and the completion claim had to be walked back into a further 5-plan expansion.
cargo fmt-on-crate-root drift recurred across nearly every executor session, requiring manual `git checkout --` reverts of out-of-scope reformatted files before each commit.
